subject.title: Intermittent 30+ minute workspace-sandbox prep on cold-start (5.19-beta.1)

question: Should this intermittent workspace-sandbox cold-start report be resolved by refreshing or replacing the Docker timeout/fail-soft PR now, or should maintainers first require finer sandbox-prep diagnostics to isolate prune, workspace layout, Docker user resolution, and backend init separately?
rationale: The issue is a real availability report, but the exact slow substep is unproven and the current candidate fix changes compatibility-sensitive timeout/default behavior while leaving adjacent wait paths in question.

options.title: Refresh or replace the timeout PR
options.body: Preserve current sandbox skill-mount behavior, bound the full Docker control-plane path that can hang, document any timeout/default surface, and require real wedged-Docker or OrbStack proof before merge.

options.title: Add diagnostics before choosing the fix
options.body: Instrument sandbox-prep substeps first so maintainers can prove whether the cold-start stalls are prune, workspace layout/skill sync, Docker user resolution, backend init, or another OrbStack-specific wait.

options.title: Track only the narrower Docker no-timeout issue
options.body: Close this broader report only if maintainers decide the remaining user problem is fully owned by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90980 and no distinct cold-start prep latency work remains.

recommendation.title: Refresh or replace the timeout PR
recommendation.body: Preserve current sandbox skill-mount behavior, bound the full Docker control-plane path that can hang, document any timeout/default surface, and require real wedged-Docker or OrbStack proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice spans sandbox architecture, prune/runtime cleanup, and compatibility-sensitive fail-soft behavior, all areas with recent history from this person.
